title: What is agentic AI? Observable classification from first question to system evidence

learnSequence.title: Name the model, product, and runtime layers
learnSequence.outcome: The learner separates a model from the interface, retrieval, memory, tools, deterministic code, and execution runtime around it.
activities: Label the layers in a familiar AI interaction without assigning every behavior to the model.
Rewrite marketing-led descriptions as observable, version-scoped statements.
masteryEvidence: A layer map that identifies observed behavior, responsible component, evidence, and unknowns.

learnSequence.title: Classify who chooses the next step
learnSequence.outcome: The learner distinguishes a model response, a code-directed workflow, an agent loop, and a complete agentic system by control flow and feedback.
activities: Trace who selects each transition in equivalent model-call, workflow, and agent examples.
Identify the loop, feedback, state, stop condition, and accountable controller.
masteryEvidence: An annotated control-flow trace with model-directed and code-directed transitions marked separately.

learnSequence.title: Locate tools, state, side effects, and human authority
learnSequence.outcome: The learner identifies which runtime executes actions, where durable state lives, how effects are verified, and which person remains accountable.
activities: Follow a tool-call proposal through validation, authorization, execution, result, and postcondition evidence.
Mark application-managed, product-managed, external, optional, absent, and unknown behavior without guessing.
masteryEvidence: A responsibility map for identity, tools, state, approvals, verification, recovery, and human authority.

learnSequence.title: Compare exact product experiences across providers
learnSequence.outcome: The learner classifies version-scoped experiences from multiple provider families without turning a product or provider name into a permanent technical claim.
activities: Compare a model endpoint with an agent product or framework inside at least four provider families.
Label each claim documented, tested, inferred, or unknown and record its review deadline.
masteryEvidence: A cited comparison table covering at least eight provider-family cases and preserving every material unknown.

learnSequence.title: Defend an agentic and multi-agent classification
learnSequence.outcome: The learner uses run evidence to justify whether a system is deterministic, single-agent, agentic, or multi-agent and rejects unnecessary complexity.
activities: Evaluate equivalent cases using deterministic, single-agent, and multi-agent designs.
Defend the least complex classification that matches observed coordination, authority, state, and recovery evidence.
masteryEvidence: A classification dossier with run trace, handoff evidence where applicable, uncertainty, corrective controls, and human disposition.

fieldGuideAssets.purpose: Give a reader a fast sequence of observable questions for deciding whether a named experience is a model, workflow, agent, or agentic system.
Compare all eight taxonomy classes without implying that a product label proves runtime behavior.
Show model-versus-harness distinctions across provider families using dated first-party evidence and explicit unknowns.
Prevent unsupported claims that a provider, model, assistant, tool-call response, or multi-model workflow is inherently agentic.
Explain learner-facing terms, synonyms, disputed marketing language, and the most common category mistakes in plain language.

requiredCompetencies: Separate a model from the product and execution harness around it.
Identify whether code or a model chooses the next executable step.
Locate tool execution, side effects, state, verification, and recovery.
Classify an exact product experience using observable evidence and unknowns.
Distinguish single-agent from multi-agent coordination using handoff evidence.
Choose the least complex accurate classification and preserve human authority.
